headline: Rocket swings to profit on higher volume and servicing scale
summary_short: Rocket Companies reported Q1 2026 revenue of $2.94B (+167% y/y) and net income of $297M, versus a $212M net loss a year earlier, as closed loan origination volume rose to $44.7B following the Redfin and Mr. Cooper acquisitions.
summary_long: Total revenue, net rose to $2.94B from $1.10B a year ago, driven by higher gain-on-sale volume, a larger servicing portfolio (servicing fee income +$682M) and interest income from custodial deposits. Net income swung to $297M from a $212M loss as revenue growth outpaced a 92% rise in total expenses, mostly compensation and acquisition-related costs tied to the Redfin and Mr. Cooper integrations. Loan origination volume reached $44.7B (+107% y/y) while gain-on-sale margin narrowed slightly to 2.74% from 2.89%. Cash and equivalents stood at $2.69B and stockholders' equity rose to $23.2B, up sharply y/y on stock issued for the two all-stock acquisitions. No forward guidance was given in the filing.

drivers.explanation: Origination volume reached $44.7B, up $23.1B y/y, as Net income swung to $297M from a $212M loss, driven by higher loan production and the Redfin and Mr. Cooper acquisitions.

Gain on sale of loans rose on higher net rate lock volume; servicing fee income grew with a larger average servicing portfolio; interest income rose on custodial deposits and higher origination volume.
Revenue growth of 167% y/y outpaced a 92% rise in total expenses ($2.54B vs $1.32B), driven by variable compensation, acquisition-related costs and interest expense on assumed debt.
Not explained in the release beyond the underlying revenue and origination-volume growth; no standalone operating-cash-flow discussion is given.
Release explains the y/y cash increase (acquired cash from the Acquisitions) but does not address the roughly flat sequential quarter-over-quarter balance.
Release explains the y/y equity increase (stock issued for Redfin and Mr. Cooper); the smaller sequential increase reflects retention of the quarter's net income.
Share count rose from all-stock consideration issued for the Redfin and Mr. Cooper acquisitions and the Up-C Collapse's conversion of Class D shares to Class A shares.
